findings.claim: A newcomer copies a reviewer file, the plugin later updates, and nothing tells them. install.sh compares only files under CLAUDE_HOME against its manifest, so 'differs, kept' never fires for a project copy, and the plugin channel has no such message. FR-003 says 're-compare after a plugin update' but gives no trigger, no command and no way to tell whether the shipped file changed. The author accepted the stale copy as 'the accepted cost'; the author is a maintainer, not the newcomer who carries it, and R-7 dogfooding covers the operator's installs, not a stranger's project. Remedy: give one diff command against the shipped file and a stated cue (any plugin update), and record that newcomers' cost was accepted on their behalf.

evidence.note: The stale copy is called the accepted cost.
FR-003 gives re-compare with no trigger or command.
The 'differs, kept' logic covers only manifest paths under CLAUDE_HOME.
The voice fork was waived by the author's ruling.

findings.pull_quote: The author who accepted the cost will never be the one who pays it.

findings.claim: FR-003 lists tools among the keys to change and spec.md:55 treats a custom list as success. Shipped personas run with all tools and write memory. A newcomer who narrows tools to save cost can strip the Write or Read access the persona's memory upkeep and JSON reply depend on. The spec has no warning, minimum tool set or check, and chorus validates no run setting (FR-001), so the reviewer degrades silently. Remedy: name in the cost statement the tools a reviewer needs, or advise model and effort first and tools only with a stated minimum.

evidence.note: A changed tools list is a success scenario with no caution.
FR-001 means nothing validates a run setting.
Shipped agents carry memory: project and use no tools key today.

findings.pull_quote: The recipe hands over the dangerous lever and keeps the label off it.
findings.need_info_reason: I did not verify which tools a persona's reply and memory writes actually need on the host.

findings.claim: The record no longer shows which reviewer ran differently. A reader of a published record cannot tell a cheaper-model dissent from a default one. The operator ruled this narrowing, so I do not re-argue it. The missed consequence: the cost lands on the record's reader, a different person from the retuner, and 'revisit with a source that is not the conductor' has no owner or trigger. Remedy: state in the README cost that records do not show a retune, and suggest the retuner note it in their project addendum.

evidence.note: Showing the difference in the record is out of scope, revisit with no owner.
The edge case states the record does not show a project copy ran.

findings.pull_quote: A record that hides who ran differently is cleaner for the builder and blinder for the reader.

findings.claim: FR-004 words the cost as 'forks the persona' and 'installer will not update it', in mechanism terms; newcomers think 'my reviewer stops improving'. The README headings a newcomer scans are Install and Run a round, and the section's position is left open. SC-003 has no task behind it. Remedy: word the cost in outcome terms, place the section next to Run a round, and give SC-003 a fresh-reader task.

evidence.note: The cost statement uses the terms fork and installer.
SC-003 has no task behind it.
Install and Run a round are where a newcomer looks.

findings.pull_quote: Say what the reader loses, not what the repository did.
